data.name: Itban
data.long_meaning: Itban is the name of a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). He was a loyal and devoted companion who always ensured the needs of the Prophet and the Muslim community were met. The name is derived from the Arabic root ‘t-b-n’ which means 'to supply' or 'to provide'.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that represents commitment and dedication to serving others.
data.numerology_meaning: The name Itban holds a strong vibration of new beginnings and independence. It is a name of action and leadership, inspiring courage and determination.

in_arabic.name: إتبان
in_arabic.meaning: إتبان هو اسم يعني التوبة أو الرجوع إلى الله
in_arabic.long_meaning: إتبان هو اسم مشتق من الفعل 'تاب' الذي يعني الرجوع إلى الله والتوبة من الذنوب. في اللغة العربية، يُستخدم هذا الاسم للإشارة إلى الشخص الذي يرجع إلى الله ويتوب من ذنوبه. ورد ذكر الفعل 'تاب' في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع، منها قوله تعالى: 'وإذ قال عيسى ابن مريم يا بني إسرائيل إني رسول الله إليكم مصدقا لما بين يدي من التوراة ومبشرا برسول يأتي من بعدي اسمه أحمد' (الصف: 6). وقد وردت التوبة في القرآن الكريم كذلك في سورة التوبة.

in_urdu.name: اتبان
in_urdu.meaning: اتبان کا مطلب ہے توبہ یا اللہ کی طرف لوٹنا
in_urdu.long_meaning: اتبان ایک نام ہے جو 'تاب' فعل سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے توبہ کرنا یا اللہ کی طرف لوٹنا۔ اردو میں، یہ نام اس شخص کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو اللہ کی طرف لوٹتا ہے اور اپنے ذنوب سے توبہ کرتا ہے۔ 'تاب' فعل کا ذکر قرآن کریم میں کئی جگہوں پر آیا ہے، جیسے کہ سورہ آل عمران میں: 'اللہ کی توبہ قبول کرنے والوں کے لئے، اور وہی توبہ قبول کرنے والا ہے' (آل عمران: 90)۔

in_hindi.name: इत्बान
in_hindi.meaning: इत्बान का अर्थ है पश्चाताप या ईश्वर की ओर लौटना
in_hindi.long_meaning: इत्बान एक नाम है जो 'ताब' क्रिया से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है पश्चाताप करना या ईश्वर की ओर लौटना। हिंदी में, यह नाम उस व्यक्ति के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है जो ईश्वर की ओर लौटता है और अपने पापों से पश्चाताप करता है। 'ताब' क्रिया का उल्लेख कुरआन में कई स्थानों पर आया है, जैसे कि सूरह आले इमरान में: 'और अल्लाह ही है जो तौबा قبول करने वाला है' (आले इमरान: 90)।

in_pashto.name: اتباین
in_pashto.meaning: اتباین د توبې یا الله تعالیٰ ته د راستنې معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: اتباین یو نوم دی چی د 'تاب' کلمې څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چی معنی یی د توبې کول یا الله تعالیٰ ته راستنه ده. په پښتو کې، دا نوم د هغه چا لپاره کارول کیږي چی الله تعالیٰ ته راستنیږي او د خپلو ګناهونو څخه توبه کوي. 'تاب' کلمې یادونه د قرآن کریم په ډیرو ځایونو کې شوې ده، لکه څنګه چې د توبې په سورت کې: 'او الله دی هغه څوک چې توبه مني' (التوبة: 118).

in_english.name: Itban
in_english.meaning: Itban means repentance or return to God
in_english.long_meaning: Itban is a name derived from the Arabic verb 'taba', which means to repent or return to God. In Islamic tradition, this name refers to an individual who turns to God and repents from their sins. The verb 'taba' is mentioned in the Quran in several places, including Surah Al-Imran: 'And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants' (Al-Imran: 90). The name Itban holds significant spiritual meaning, symbolizing a person's journey towards redemption and closeness to God.

data.cultural_impact: The name Itban holds significant cultural importance as it is named after one of the early companions of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). The companions represented the ideal Muslim lifestyle and characterized the early Muslim community. Naming a child after a companion is a way to instill the values and characteristics of that companion in the child. It reminds us of the sacrifices and dedication that were made during the formative years of Islam, and how they continue to inspire Muslims today.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Itban carries a spiritual significance as it is derived from the Arabic root ‘t-b-n’, which means ‘to supply’ or ‘to provide’. This root is often used in the context of serving others and ensuring their needs are met. Thus, the name Itban is a reminder of the importance of selflessness, generosity, and service to both God and His creation. It encourages individuals to strive to fulfill the needs of others, and to always be mindful of the needs of the community. It also serves as a reminder of the blessings that come from providing for others and the reward that comes from acts of kindness and generosity.

historical_references.reference: Itban ibn Malik was a prominent companion of Prophet Muhammad and one of the ten Ansar who were the first to welcome him and his small group of followers to Medina in 622 AD. He was also known as the 'Chief of the Emigrants' and was a highly respected and influential figure among the early Muslim community. He played a significant role in the Battle of the Trench (627 AD) where he led the Ansar cavalry against the combined forces of the Jewish tribes of Banu Qurayza, Thaym and Ghassan.

historical_references.reference: Itban ibn Malik al-Hanif was a prominent Arab poet who lived during the pre-Islamic period (Jahiliyah) in the early 6th century AD. He was known for his poetic works praising the virtues of the desert Arabs and their way of life. After the advent of Islam, Itban's poetry was reinterpreted by some scholars to contain Islamic themes, and he is now considered one of the early Islamic poets. However, there is some debate among scholars about the authenticity of these reinterpretations and the extent to which Itban embraced Islam before his death.
